newsitem.title: USA: Indianapolis council approves United plan.
newsitem.headline: Indianapolis council approves United plan.

text.p: The Indianapolis City Council has approved a new plan for paying off $140 million of lease revenue bonds issued in 1991 as part of its share of funding for a maintenance facility for UAL Corp's United Airlines.

Indianapolis had pledged revenues from its county option income tax to finance the debt, which was sold through the Indianapolis Local Public Improvement Bond Bank, for its share of the $1 billion project.

Revenue from the tax funds police, fire and other public safety programs, however, and Indianapolis officials have avoided using it to fund the debt service, said Bob Swintz, deputy director of the Indianapolis local bond bank.

The combination of revenue sources used over the last six years will not be available next year, however, and without some changes, Indianapolis would have to begin using part of the county option income tax, Swintz said.

Under the plan approved Monday night by the city council, the debt will continue to have the support of the general obligation county option income tax, but will be financed through revnues generated by a consolidated TIF district and an increase in the general obligation property tax, Swintz said.

To avoid a tax increase, the city plan reduces the general obligation property tax levy backing sanitary district bonds by a corresponding amount, Swintz said. An increase in sanitary district revenues will be used to replace the debt service taken away, he added.
The consolidated TIF district is expected to provide about $4.5 million per year for debt service, which has ranged from $8 million to $12 million, Swintz said.
Under Indiana law, amendments to public bond issues have a notice period for public comment before the state board of tax commissioners considers them for final approval, Swintz said.

Indianpolis officials hope to receive final approval by the end of June for the plan, which would then be incorporated into the 1998 city budget to be formally introduced to the city council in August, Swintz said.
